fixes.explanation: That's what he does, baker. When he hears that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he begins to cry out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” (Mark 10:47). He calls Jesus by name and asks for mercy, out loud. No mumbling here.
Nope, no messenger here, friend. Bartimaeus doesn't send anybody. He calls out himself, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” (Mark 10:47). The text has him crying out, and that's the whole move.

Waiting would've been the quiet move, friend. But the text says that when he heard it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out (Mark 10:47). Nothing in the story has him waiting for the crowd to pass. He starts crying out.

That's the opposite of what happens, baker. The text says many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder (Mark 10:48). They said hush, and he got LOUDER. He didn't quiet down.
Right on, baker. Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” (Mark 10:49). A large crowd is with Him, and still He stops. Then He has Bartimaeus called over.

That's it, baker. They called the blind man and said, “Take courage!” and “Get up! He is calling for you.” (Mark 10:49). Jesus is the one calling for him, and those words carry the news. Good news deserves a little cheering.
Staying put isn't what they say, friend. They tell him, “Take courage!” and “Get up! He is calling for you.” (Mark 10:49). There's no word about waiting. Jesus is calling for him.
True. The text says, “Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus.” (Mark 10:50). He throws off his cloak and he JUMPS. I wish I moved like that when my oven timer goes off.
Flip that one, baker. The text says that throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus (Mark 10:50). Jesus was calling for him, and up he went. He jumped.
Yep, see. He says, “Rabboni, let me see again.” (Mark 10:51). Jesus asked what he wanted, and Bartimaeus tells Him plainly. He asks to see again.
Walking isn't what he asks for, friend. He says, “Rabboni, let me see again.” (Mark 10:51). Jesus asks what he wants, and the answer is about sight. He asks to see again.

Heading back into Jericho isn't what the text says, friend. Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho (Mark 10:46). Bartimaeus followed Jesus along the road (Mark 10:52). That's where the story leaves him.

A fine idea if I'd written it, baker, but the text doesn't go there. It says he “…followed Jesus along the road.” (Mark 10:52). We aren't told he runs off to tell anyone. We only hear that he follows Jesus.
